blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Ocean waves, tides, currents, and sea-level fluctuations are the major forces shaping coastal topography.
High rocky coasts are dominated by erosional landforms such as sea cliffs, wave-cut platforms, sea caves, arches, and stacks.
Low sedimentary coasts are dominated by depositional landforms including beaches, bars, spits, lagoons, and tombolos.
Emergent coastlines result from land upliftment or falling sea levels, typically displaying raised beaches and wave-cut terraces.
Submergent coastlines form due to land subsidence or rising sea levels, creating rias, fjords, and dalmatian coasts.

blocks.content: Waves are the most dominant force in shaping coastal landforms, driving both erosional processes and sediment deposition.

items: Distinction between India's East Coast (emergent nature, depositional features) and West Coast (submergent nature in north/central, erosional & estuary features) is a frequently asked geography topic.
Differentiate clearly between Ria coasts (drowned river valleys) and Fjord coasts (drowned glaciated valleys).
Sequence of erosional landforms: Sea Cave -> Sea Arch -> Stack -> Stump is highly tested in objective questions.
